\paragraph{Comparison with common prompts.}
The accuracy panels of Fig.~\ref{fig:hosted-verified-breadth} and the
\texttt{pass@8}/\texttt{distinct@8} columns of
Table~\ref{tab:hosted-level-averages-medium} use normalized grading, with
revised \texttt{Python} wording for Claude Opus 5. The lower figure panels and the
table's \pmd{} columns instead use strict grading and original wording.
Table~\ref{tab:hosted-level-averages-parity}
compares normalized success and mode counts over \texttt{Graph}, \texttt{Countdown}, \texttt{MathIR} and \texttt{PantryPlan},
the four domains with identical prompts across deployments.
Claude Opus 5 averages 1.42/1.45/1.35 verified modes
at Levels 1--3, compared with 1.43/1.44/1.36 over five
domains using revised \texttt{Python} wording and 1.36/1.17/1.08
using original \texttt{Python} wording. It has the lowest mean \texttt{distinct@8} at
each level in all three comparisons. The revised condition increases its verified
\texttt{Python} mode count, which also depends on response success; these means do not
compare diversity at matched accuracy. The ordering of the other deployments
depends on whether \texttt{Python} is included.

A separate \texttt{Python} comparison in App.~\ref{app:sampling-budget-effects} uses
original and neutral wording on three deployments,
with 16 prompts and 64
responses per prompt at Levels 2 and 3. Pair-pooled diversity $1-C$ rises by
+.024 to +.131 across its
six deployment--level cells; the largest value under either
wording is .369 (effective-mode transform
1.58). These values weight correct pairs equally,
unlike promptwise \pmd{}. They describe that neutral-wording comparison and
do not bound the effect of other wordings or the revised no-system condition
on untested deployments.
